newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire officer jailed for trading arms to rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire officer jailed for trading arms to rebels.

text.p: Two senior Zairean army officers have been jailed, one for abandoning his post and the other for trading arms to rebels in exchange for cows and gold, army officers said on Friday.
They said a military tribunal in the capital Kinshasa jailed a colonel, who commanded an infantry battalion in Fizi in South Kivu province, for life on Thursday for trading arms to rebels.
It jailed a gendarmerie battalion commander at the eastern lake port of Kalemie for 30 months for abandoning his post.
The tribunal, made up of military magistrates and senior officers, acquitted two other senior officers on Friday for lack of evidence.
One risked the death penalty after being charged with selling maize destined for his troops in Kalemie in November.
The second was accused of stealing vehicles and taking a Rwandan woman as a lover in defiance of military regulations banning soldiers from marrying foreigners.

The senior court clerk said all four cases would go to appeal -- two challenged by the defence and two by the prosecution. A fifth officer awaits trial. All have been held in a Kinshasa military jail since the start of the year.

A military tribunal in the eastern city of Kisangani sentenced 14 Zairean soldiers to death in January for cowardice. Court sources say the 14 have appealed to President Mobutu Sese Seko for clemency.
Zaire's notoriously undisciplined army has since October been driven back by rebels advancing from the east.
